'''Smadar Naoz''' ({{Langx|he|סמדר נאוז}}; born 1978)<ref name=meet>{{cite web|url=https://www.ynet.co.il/home/0,7340,L-7895,00.html |title=Meet astrophysicist Smadar Naoz (in Hebrew) |publisher=Ynet |author=Galit Roichman}}</ref> is an [[Israeli-American]] [[astrophysicist]], and was the 2015 winner of the [[Annie Jump Cannon Award in Astronomy]] for her scientific contributions to the fields of [[cosmology]] and [[orbital mechanics|planetary dynamics]].<ref>{{cite web | url = https://aas.org/grants-and-prizes/annie-jump-cannon-award-astronomy | publisher = [[American Astronomical Society]] | author = Annie J. Cannon Award Committee | title = Annie Jump Cannon Award in Astronomy}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.livescience.com/16187-galaxies-nsf-sl-naoz.html | publisher = [[Live Science]] | title = Astrophysicist Unfolds Mysteries of First Galaxies | date = 22 September 2011 | author = Smadar Naoz}}</ref>

==Early life and education ==
Naoz grew up in [[Jerusalem|Jerusalem, Israel]], and developed her love for astrophysics at a young age with her mother regularly watching [[Star Trek: The Original Series]] with her and her younger sister.<ref name=meet/> She graduated from the Racah Institute at [[The Hebrew University]] with her Bachelors of Science (2002) and her Masters in Science (2004), before continuing her education at the [[Tel Aviv University]], where she was awarded her PhD in 2010. The subject of her PhD research was the first generation of galaxies.<ref name=meet/><ref name=Phd>{{cite book|title=The first generation of galaxies and 21 cm fluctuations |oclc = 713757374}}</ref>

==Career==
After obtaining her PhD, Naoz accepted an IAU Gruber postdoctoral fellowship at [[Northwestern University]]'s Center for Interdisciplinary Exploration and Research in Astrophysics (CIERA). After her tenure as an IAU Gruber postdoc, she became an Einstein Fellow at the Institute for Theory and Computation at the [[Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics|Center for Astrophysics {{!}} Harvard & Smithsonian]] in [[Cambridge, Massachusetts]].<ref name=Naoz>{{cite web | url = http://www.astro.ucla.edu/~snaoz/Smadarcv.pdf | author = Smadar Naoz | title = Curriculum Vitae | date = February 2016 }}</ref>

Naoz is continuing her research, and working as an assistant professor at the Department of Physics and Astronomy at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.astro.ucla.edu/~snaoz/ | author = Smadar Naoz | title = Welcome to Smadar Naoz's website | date = 2016}}</ref>

==Research==
Naoz  started her career investigating the formation of the [[Galaxy formation and evolution|first generation of galaxies]] following the creation of the universe, contributing to cosmology by trying to piece together early structure formation.<ref name=Naoz2>{{cite web | url = http://www.astro.ucla.edu/~snaoz/FGalaxies.html | author = Smadar Naoz | title = The First Galaxies in the Universe: the Contribution of Gas }}</ref>

Naoz has been probing the dynamical evolution of [[Hot Jupiter]]s. She has published many papers in leading scientific journals,<ref name=papers>{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=XDXbVfMAAAAJ&hl=en |title=Smadar Naoz on google scholar |access-date=August 16, 2018 |publisher=google scholar}}</ref> including a paper about Hot Jupiters interactions, in the science journal [[Nature (journal)|Nature]].<ref name=nature>{{cite journal
|journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]|title=Hot Jupiters from secular planet–planet interactions|first1=Smadar|last1=Naor|first2=Will M.|last2=Farr|first3=Yoram|last3=Lithwick|first4=Fredrick A. |last4=Rasio |first5=Jean |last5=Teyssandier |volume=473 |pages=187–189|date=May 12, 2011|number=7346|doi=10.1038/nature10076|pmid=21562558|arxiv=1011.2501|bibcode=2011Natur.473..187N |s2cid=4424942 }}</ref>

==Awards==
* [[Fellow of the American Physical Society]], 2022<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2022|title=Fellows nominated in 2022|work=APS Fellows archive|publisher=American Physical Society|access-date=2022-10-19}}</ref>
* [[Helen B. Warner Prize for Astronomy]] awarded by the American Astronomical Society, 2020
* [[Annie Jump Cannon Award in Astronomy|Annie Jump Cannon Prize]] awarded by the American Astronomical Society, 2015<ref name=Naoz/>
* Einstein Fellowship awarded by NASA, Sept. 2012<ref name=Naoz/>
* The National Postdoctoral Award Program for Advancing Women in Science, awarded by [[Weizmann Institute of Science]], 2009-2011<ref name=Naoz/>
* [[Dan David Prize]] 2009 scholarship recipient in the field of "Astrophysics – History of the Universe"<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dandavidprize.org/scholars/2009/132-past-astrophysics,-history-of-the-universe/330-naoz-smadar |title=SCHOLARS 2009 |publisher= Dan David prize |access-date=August 16, 2018}}</ref>
* The [[Gruber Foundation|Peter and Patricia Gruber Foundation Fellowship]] in 2010.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.iau.org/news/announcements/detail/ann10014/ | publisher = [[International Astronomical Union]] | title = Peter and Patrica Gruber Foundation Fellowship 2010 awarded to Smadar Naoz | date = 13 April 2010 }}</ref>
* School of Physics and Astronomy Award for Outstanding Achievements, awarded by Tel Aviv University, 2006<ref name=Naoz/>
